PullRequest.Title: chat: clarify session storage paths in sandbox confirmations
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #347564
Related to #347248 (parent issue).

## Summary

Sandbox grant confirmations currently expose opaque SDK session IDs in storage paths. Users recognize their session names, not those directory IDs.

- Add a reusable, sandbox-independent session-path display helper, adopted only by sandbox confirmations in this change.
- Describe current-session files as, for example, **Allow read access to `files/workspace.yml` in this session's storage.** Use the current title for another known session, and preserve raw paths when ownership or a usable title is unavailable.
- Resolve ownership from known chat backings at display time, including multiple chats, descendants, moves, promotion and renames. Chat storage paths themselves do not move.
- When a blocked file leads to a broader grant, explicitly name the actual grant path. Original tool Input may describe the blocked file rather than the granted folder.
- Preserve authorization targets, read/write semantics, Allow/Skip actions, Input, terminal commands and persistence warnings. No Full Path expander is added.

Entirely unknown or unmaterialized sessions retain their raw paths; this does not scan storage or infer ownership from an SDK ID.

## Coverage

Tests cover path boundaries and normalization, host-specific path comparisons, ambiguous ownership, missing titles, custom storage roots, mapped resources, current/other sessions, peer and descendant chats, ownership transfers, promotion, renames and broader grants. Production chat-widget fixtures cover generic and terminal confirmations, narrow layouts and themes.

- Focused helper, formatter, runtime, ownership and title tests: **18 passed**.
- ESLint: **all 12 changed TypeScript files passed**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Full integration and smoke suites were not run.

## How to Test

1. Trigger a sandbox read or write confirmation for a nested file in the current session's storage. Verify the session-aware wording preserves the relative path and Input remains unchanged.
2. Request access to a known named session's storage from another session. Verify its title is shown. Move a chat or rename its owning session, then trigger a fresh confirmation and verify the label reflects the current owner/title.
3. Trigger a folder grant for a blocked file. Verify the explanation identifies the actual granted path, even when Input contains only the requested file.
4. Verify unknown paths remain absolute, terminal confirmations retain their commands, and Allow/Skip and persistence behavior are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a sandbox path-grant confirmation for a read or shell tool targeting current-session, peer-session, or unknown storage
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The SDK permission callback builds the pending confirmation; the diff synchronously snapshots materialized chat roots, resolves titles, normalizes paths, and formats the label before emitting pending_confirmation. This work is on confirmation-display latency, but it does not wait on any new expensive boundary.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One or two displayed paths per grant (grant path plus optional denied path), each scanning the currently materialized Copilot chat backings. Effective cost is O(P × C), where P is at most 2 and C is loaded chat backings; typical C is small and the operations are map lookups, URI construction, normalization, and short-lived allocations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Permission requests may be concurrent across live sessions; there is no shared limiter or coalescing for label computation, so aggregate local CPU scales with concurrent confirmations. Each individual computation is synchronous and lightweight, and no new asynchronous fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Ownership and title data are deliberately read fresh so chat moves, promotion, and renames are reflected. Cold and warm behavior are the same in-memory O(C) scan; there is no filesystem-derived discovery, cache miss, or negative-cache retry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the O(P × C) synchronous allocation/normalization mechanism and its critical-path placement; low confidence that its magnitude is user-visible at realistic loaded-chat counts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A process can accumulate more materialized chats, but the reviewed code provides no evidence of a realistic cardinality at which these in-memory scans would materially delay an already user-gated confirmation. Exact duration is unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds repeated in-memory work, including a second root snapshot when deniedPath exists, but no expensive boundary and no sufficiently evidenced latency, throughput, memory, or GC impact under a realistic trigger.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a sandbox path-grant confirmation for a write request with an edit preview
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before the changed label formatting runs, the existing permission flow checks whether the target file exists and writes the proposed content to the pending-edit-content in-memory filesystem. The diff then performs the same local root/title/path formatting as the read/shell scenario before emitting the confirmation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check whether the existing edit target exists through IFileService
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One exists call per eligible write permission request
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same existence check was already on the write-confirmation path before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the confirmation is emitted so the preview can identify a new file

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write proposed content to the pending-edit-content in-memory filesystem
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One in-memory write per eligible write permission request
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same in-memory preview write was already on the write-confirmation path before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the confirmation is emitted so the client can fetch the after-content

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One target file and one in-memory preview per eligible write request; changed label work scans C materialized chat backings for one or two grant paths. There is no collection-sized filesystem fan-out introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent write permission requests can overlap. Existing file checks and in-memory writes are not newly parallelized or serialized by this change; the new formatting is synchronous per request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The pre-existing edit preview does not use a result cache. Session ownership/title formatting intentionally reads current in-memory state, with identical cold and warm behavior and no boundary cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that all transitive boundary calls are pre-existing and that the diff adds only local computation after them.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote or virtual file-provider latency for the pre-existing exists call varies, but the PR neither adds nor moves that call. The added local scan is not evidenced as material relative to that existing path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing filesystem work remains unchanged in cardinality and placement; the diff adds bounded in-memory formatting only.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open chat accessibility help after the new sandbox-session explanation is added
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accessibility help text is assembled synchronously when help is requested; the diff appends one localized static sentence. No startup, render-loop, input-loop, IPC, filesystem, database, subprocess, or network boundary is added.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work: one additional localized string and one array append per help-text construction.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Runs within the single help invocation; no queue, fan-out, or concurrency change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No relevant cache or cache-key behavior is changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed function and static localization call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the added constant work is negligible.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and all diff pages. Traced sandbox confirmation formatting through chat ownership/title lookup, URI normalization, permission emission, and the pre-existing write-preview filesystem path; also checked accessibility-help construction. No high-confidence actionable performance issue was introduced, and the PR is not itself a demonstrated shipped-regression fix.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
